title: Introducing Plivo CLI for voice agents
summary: Connect and debug voice agents with Plivo CLI. Configure Audio Streaming or SIP trunking, test WebSocket audio, and diagnose calls from your terminal.
body_markdown:
Getting a voice agent onto a phone call is the part that pulls you out of your editor. You configure the connection in one console tab and attach a number in another. Then a call fails, you get a hangup code, and you guess.


Today we are releasing Plivo CLI, a command line interface to the Plivo APIs, built for developers shipping voice agents and for the coding agents working alongside them.


There are two common ways to put a voice agent on the phone network, and the CLI covers both:


- **Audio Streaming:** Your agent speaks WebSocket. Plivo streams the call’s audio to it and, on a bidirectional stream, plays back the audio it sends.
- **SIP trunking:** Your agent speaks SIP. Plivo routes calls to it over a trunk.


Either way you keep the stack you already have and use Plivo for the connection to real calls.


## Install and log in


```text
brew   install   plivo/tap/plivo
plivo   login
```


One binary, no runtime. macOS, Linux and Windows, with Scoop and shell installers in the[installation guide](https://www.plivo.com/docs/cli/install) . Login happens in your browser, so your password never touches the CLI.


## Stream call audio to your agent


Test your WebSocket connection before attaching a phone number, then take real calls on your local agent.


- **Test:**` plivo voice streams test` sends Plivo-format audio and counts replies. A live call still checks whether the returned audio plays correctly.
- **Forward:**` plivo voice streams forward` tunnels inbound call audio to your laptop, with no tunnel account needed. Use a test application.


Start with the[Pipecat guide](https://www.plivo.com/docs/voice-agents/audio-streaming/integration-guides/pipecat) .


## Connect your agent over SIP


Manage the Plivo side of your SIP connection from the terminal:


- **Connect:** Create trunks, manage authentication and attach phone numbers with` plivo sip` and` plivo numbers` .
- **Inspect:** Read SIP call records for hangup causes and transport details when a call fails.


Configure routing to your agent on the platform too. The[LiveKit setup guide](https://www.plivo.com/docs/voice-agents/sip-trunking/integration-guides/livekit) covers both sides.


## Get answers without leaving the terminal


Use` plivo ask` for questions about building with Plivo. For an Audio Streaming or other Voice API call,` diagnose` explains what happened, the likely cause and what to change.


```text
plivo   ask   "How do I stream call audio to my WebSocket server?"
plivo   voice   calls   diagnose   <  call_uui  d  >
```


For SIP calls, inspect the call record with` plivo sip calls get` .


## Give your coding agent the context


Bundled skills teach your coding agent how to use the CLI, Audio Streaming, SIP trunking and Voice XML. They install locally with no network call.


```text
plivo   skill   install   all
```


The CLI also supports JSON output for API commands,` --dry-run` previews and explicit confirmation for commands that spend money.


## Get started


Choose[WebSocket](https://www.plivo.com/docs/voice-agents/audio-streaming/overview) or[SIP trunking](https://www.plivo.com/docs/voice-agents/sip-trunking/overview) , then use the[CLI](https://www.plivo.com/docs/cli/overview) to connect your agent.


Plivo CLI is open source under Apache 2.0. Tell us how it goes with` plivo feedback` , or file an issue on[the repository](https://github.com/plivo/plivo-cli) .
